newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan police kill accused kidnapper in gunbattle.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan police kill accused kidnapper in gunbattle.

text.p: Taiwan police on Tuesday shot and killed a man suspected of kidnapping and murdering the teenage daughter of a popular actress in a crime that triggered mass protests and caused several top officials to resign.
One officer was killed and three others were wounded during the gunfight. A passer-by was also wounded, police said.
Police identified the dead suspect as Lin Chun-sheng and said he was shot 10 times in the gunbattle and died on the way to hospital, police said.
Two other suspects escaped the blockade, police added.
A live television broadcast of the gunbattle showed dozens of officers with bullet-proof vests exchanging fire with the gunmen while hundreds of people stopped to watch.

Authorities said they had rushed in more than 500 armed police to confront the three suspects, sought for the abduction and murder in April of Pai Hsiao-yen, the 17-year-old daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping.
Pai Hsiao-yen, whose father was the late Japanese comic book artist Ikki Kajiwara, was kidnapped on April 14 on her way to school.
Her kidnappers chopped off half of her left little finger, sent it to her mother and demanded a US$5 million ransom.
The kidnappers aborted a planned meeting with the mother after learning she had reported the case to police. The girl's body was later found floating in a river. She had been strangled.

The killing was the latest in a spate of high-profile crimes on this affluent island, from the gangland-style execution of a local government head and his seven visitors at his house to the assassination of an opposition leader.
Police said the same trio of kidnappers suspected of killing Pai Hsiao-yen abducted a businessman in August and made off with a T$4 million (US$143,000) ransom.
The crimes triggered several street protests against a perceived breakdown of social order and prompted the resignation of Taiwan's top police superintendent and interior minister.
